cases.name: client-relative person presence contract
cases.scenario: Review the person-presence contract for group members observed across local discovery, routed discovery, and federated post-office directories. Judge the Person presence contract section, not unrelated topology scenarios.
rubric: Online and Offline are observations of the current client; recent history is secondary and never-observed people receive no invented timestamp.
Presence distinguishes eligible public local, routed, directory and authenticated observations from private routes, membership, cached routes, receipts and relay custody.
Group counts use accepted distinct verified accounts, exclude pending/removed members and infrastructure, include running accepted self, and report unresolved devices separately.
Explains source overlap, source versus physical location, discovery versus TCP/delivery success, and the absence of transitive A-B-C presence guarantees.
Lists source-specific expiry and original directory expiry preservation, legacy freshness limitations, failed-refresh aging and recovery.

cases.name: account and accepted-member presence aggregation
cases.scenario: Review only the supplied desktop presence projection. Assume the called core certificate/admission APIs enforce their documented existing contracts. Judge whether its aggregation and publication preserve person/device/evidence distinctions.
rubric: Uses fresh per-source evidence rather than peer last_seen or routes alone to establish online status.
Groups by verified account identity, retains device evidence, excludes post-office infrastructure, and does not merge names or IP addresses.
Rechecks current device/account association; gives unbound identities an explicit device-scoped key.
Group summaries exclude pending members, deduplicate accounts, include accepted current self, and keep unresolved device membership separate.
Reuses a shared roster snapshot, performs no per-member dial, propagates snapshot errors, and rejects replacement runtime publication.

cases.name: frontend expiry failure and ownership safeguards
cases.scenario: Review the shared presence store as a small state machine. Native observations supply source-specific remaining lifetime and optional history. Judge frontend handling of silence, failed IPC, overlapping responses, owner changes, and group counters.
rubric: Ages evidence independently and removes expired device evidence even without a successful refresh; recent history does not become a third primary state.
Failed/malformed top-level refreshes produce an unavailable indication instead of an empty successful map; valid recovery clears that indication.
Prevents older successful or failed responses and obsolete owner/runtime polling sessions from overwriting newer accepted state.
Bounds outstanding refreshes and retained history, clears state on stop/replacement, and preserves unchanged record references.
Uses account member keys to recompute group online counts after expiry, not a group-level online boolean; offline labels retain available observation history.

cases.name: directory origin freshness and compatibility
cases.scenario: Review directory freshness metadata, federation forwarding and the explicitly negotiated v4 response. Trusted relays report original origin expiry; clients must not renew it by re-querying.
rubric: Federated export/import retain original remote expiry and reject expired or excessive-lifetime remote proofs.
Local directory observations have bounded lifetime and require authenticated visible self presence with a valid account proof.
v4 response is explicitly versioned and preserves origin expiry with bounded pagination and valid identity proofs.
Legacy directory response layouts remain compatible but omit eligible freshness metadata; response assembly rejects mixing legacy and freshness pages.
Valid expiry becomes a monotonic client deadline and unusable freshness cannot establish online status; gateway provenance remains separate from ordinary device presence.
